verdict: Starbucks revenue was flat at $9.4B as comparable sales fell 4% on fewer customer visits, and net earnings fell 24% to $781M as higher store labor costs squeezed margins.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales fell 4%, with 8% fewer transactions partly offset by a 4% higher average ticket.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — comparable sales fell 4%, with China down 6% on a lower average ticket and fewer transactions.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — support centers and head office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment.

takeaways.title: Fewer visits, bigger tickets
takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales fell 4% — 6% fewer transactions partly offset by a 3% higher average ticket. North America fell 4% and China 6%, and total revenue slipped 0.3% to $9.4B despite 377 net new stores (40,576 in all).

takeaways.title: Store costs ate the margin
takeaways.text: Store operating expenses jumped to 54.0% of company-operated store revenue from 49.7% a year ago, on labor investment and lost leverage from lower sales; operating margin narrowed to 11.9% from 15.8%.

takeaways.title: Profit fell by a quarter
takeaways.text: Net earnings fell 24% to $781M and EPS to $0.69 from $0.90, as the margin squeeze outweighed a lower tax bill. This was the first full quarter under CEO Brian Niccol's 'Back to Starbucks' plan to win back customers.

otherDetail: Income from equity investees of $47M and $28M of interest and other income, less $127M of interest expense.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $1,122M includes $47M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income. Net earnings of $781M are essentially all attributable to Starbucks (noncontrolling interests took $0.1M). Segment revenues are rounded to whole millions; Corporate & other carries a $1M rounding difference so segments sum to total revenue.
